metadata.title: Further Spectral Properties of the Weighted Finite Fourier Transform Operator and Approximation in Weighted Sobolev Spaces.

extraction_notes.note: Theorem 2 in the introduction is a verbatim restatement of Theorem 3 (same \label keys Eq3.1/newdecay); it and its two equations get no node. The proof of Lemma 3 cites \ref{Eq3.1}, which the facts resolve to the introduction copy, so the uses edge EP13->PP6 was added by hand.

Theorem 1 (introduction) announces the main approximation result but differs from Theorem 5 in hypotheses ($c>1$ vs $c>0$) and constants, so it was kept as its own theorem rather than dropped as a restated copy; linked by a uses edge from TP12.

Section 2 restates the Jacobi-weighted Sobolev space $H^r_\alpha(I)$ (already defined in the introduction, DP5) and the introduction states the relation $\lambda_n=\frac{c}{2\pi}|\mu_n|^2$ (kept in Section 2, DP9); the duplicate copies got no node.

The GPSWFs/weighted finite Fourier transform are defined twice (intro, Section 2), each with its own numbered equation; both kept since the env-fact rule requires the equations and they define different emphases (GPSWFs vs. the operator with $\omega_\alpha$).
PSWFs are defined as solutions of an energy maximization problem; typed definition (it defines the term PSWF) rather than problem.

Many sentences end at displays without periods, so several prose nodes and steps end at a display; the proof of Proposition 1 uses an undefined $B$ and stops before deriving the stated lower bound, hence rigor semi_formal on PrP1. Duplicate \label keys (ineq, 8) occur in Theorem 1, Theorem 5 and Proposition 2.
Remark 2 states a cited norm comparison from Wang-Zhang plus commentary; kept as remark with origin external.
Figures and the table of Weierstrass-Mandelbrot approximation errors (Section 5) are numerical output, not extracted as nodes.

nodes.name: Prolate spheroidal wave functions (PSWFs)
nodes.statement: These PSWFs are defined as the solutions of the following energy maximization problem : \begin{equation*} \mbox{ Find } g=\arg\max_{f\in B_c}\frac{\int_{-1}^1|f(t)|^2 dt}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(t)|^2 dt} \end{equation*} Where $B_c$ is the classical Paley-Winer space, defined by \begin{equation} B_c=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c]\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: PSWFs are the maximizers of the energy concentration on $[-1,1]$ among functions in the Paley-Wiener space $B_c$.

nodes.name: Classical Paley-Wiener space $B_c$
nodes.statement: B_c=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c]\}.
nodes.label: Bc

nodes.name: Fourier transform $\widehat f$
nodes.statement: Here, $\widehat f$ is the Fourier transform of $f\in L^2(\mathbb R),$ defined by ${\displaystyle \widehat f(\xi)=\lim_{A\rightarrow +\infty}\int_{[-A,A]} e^{-i x\xi} f(x)\, dx.}$

nodes.name: PSWFs as eigenfunctions of the sinc kernel operator and the commuting differential operator
nodes.statement: Moreover, it has been shown in \cite{Slepian1}, that the PSWFs are also the eigenfunctions of the integral operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c}$ defined on $L^2(-1,1)$ by $${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 \frac{\sin(c(x-y))}{\pi(x-y)} f(y)\, dy} $$ as well as the eigenfunctions of a commuting differential operator $ \mathcal{L}_c$ with $ \mathcal{Q}_c$ and given by $$ \mathcal L_c f(x)= (1-x^2)f''(x)-2x f'(x) - c^2 x^2 f(x) $$
conclusions: the PSWFs are also the eigenfunctions of the integral operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c}$ defined on $L^2(-1,1)$ by $${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 \frac{\sin(c(x-y))}{\pi(x-y)} f(y)\, dy} $$ as well as the eigenfunctions of a commuting differential operator $ \mathcal{L}_c$ with $ \mathcal{Q}_c$
nodes.statement_short: PSWFs are eigenfunctions both of the sinc-kernel integral operator $\mathcal Q_c$ and of the commuting differential operator $\mathcal L_c$.

nodes.name: Generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs)
nodes.statement: In this paper, we are interested in a weighted family of PSWFs called the generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs), recently given in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} and\cite{Wang2} . They are defined as the eigenfunctions of the Gegenbauer perturbed differential operator, \begin{equation*} \mathcal L^{(\alpha)}_c \varphi(x)= (1-x^2)\varphi''(x)-2\left(\alpha+1\right)x\varphi'(x) - c^2 x^2 \varphi(x)= \mathcal L_0 \varphi(x)-c^2 x^2 \varphi(x), \mbox{ where } \alpha>-1; c>0, \end{equation*} as well as the eigenfunctions of the following commuting weighted finite Fourier transform integral operator, \begin{equation} {\displaystyle \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,(1-y^2)^{\alpha}\, dy,\, \alpha > -1.} \end{equation}
nodes.origin_citation: Karoui & Souabni 2016 (J. Fourier Anal. Appl.); Wang & Zhang 2010
differentia: the eigenfunctions of the Gegenbauer perturbed differential operator
the eigenfunctions of the following commuting weighted finite Fourier transform integral operator
nodes.statement_short: GPSWFs: eigenfunctions of the Gegenbauer-perturbed operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ and of the weighted finite Fourier transform $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$.

nodes.name: Weighted finite Fourier transform integral operator
nodes.statement: {\displaystyle \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,(1-y^2)^{\alpha}\, dy,\, \alpha > -1.}
nodes.label: integraloperator

nodes.name: Truncated GPSWFs projection $S_N$
nodes.statement: In this work, we further study the convergence rate of the projection ${\displaystyle S_N \cdot f = \displaystyle \sum_{k=0}^N <f,\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}> \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} }$ to $f$ .

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $H^r_\alpha(I)$
nodes.statement:
Here $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ are the GPSWFs and $ f \in H^s_{\alpha}(I),$ a weighted Sobolev space defined by: $$ H^r_{\alpha }(I) = \{f \in L^2_{I,\omega} : 
orm{f}_{\alpha, r}<\infty \} \quad \mbox{where} \quad 
orm{f}^2_{\alpha,r} = \displaystyle{\sum_{k=0}^r 
orm{f^{(k)}}_{\omega}^2} $$ equipped with the norm and semi-norm $$
orm{f}_{\alpha,r} = \displaystyle{\sum_{k=0}^r 
orm{f^{(k)}}_{\omega}^2} \quad \mbox{and} \quad |f|_{\alpha,r} = \|f^{(k)}\|_{\omega_{\alpha}} $$
nodes.statement_short: $H^r_\alpha(I)$: functions in the weighted $L^2$ space whose derivatives up to order $r$ have finite weighted norm.

nodes.name: Jacobi weight $\omega_\alpha$
nodes.statement: Here $$ \omega_\alpha(t) = (1-t^2)^{\alpha} \mbox{ and } \norm{.}_{\omega} = \norm{.}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} $$

nodes.name: Approximation by GPSWFs in weighted Sobolev spaces (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Let $c>1$ and $\alpha >0$, then there exist constants $K>0$ and $a>0$ such that, when $N > m_{\alpha}c$ with $m_{\alpha}=4.13\left(1.28+\frac{2\alpha+1}{1.9}\right)^{0.55}$ and $f \in H^s_{\alpha}$; $s > 0$, we have the inequality \begin{eqnarray} \|f-S_N(f)\|_{L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha})} &\leq& \left(1+ \left(\frac{N}{2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-s}{2}} \|f\|_{H^s_{\alpha}} +K.e^{-a N}\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} \end{eqnarray} Where $S_N(f)(t)=\displaystyle{\sum_{n<N}}<f,\psi_{n,c}^{\alpha}>_{L^2_{\alpha}(I)}\psi_{n,c}^{\alpha}$
conclusions: there exist constants $K>0$ and $a>0$ such that
nodes.statement_short: For $N > m_\alpha c$, the GPSWF truncation error of $f\in H^s_\alpha$ is $O(N^{-s})\|f\|_{H^s_\alpha}$ plus an exponentially small term.

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: \|f-S_N(f)\|_{L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha})} &\leq& \left(1+ \left(\frac{N}{2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-s}{2}} \|f\|_{H^s_{\alpha}} +K.e^{-a N}\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}
nodes.label: ineq

nodes.name: Weighted finite Fourier transform operator $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: The GPSWFs are defined as the eigenfunctions of the weighted finite Fourier transform operator $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},$ defined by \begin{equation} \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,\omega_{\alpha}(y)\, dy,\quad \omega_{\alpha}(y)=(1-y^2)^{\alpha},\quad \alpha >0 \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (5)
nodes.statement: \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,\omega_{\alpha}(y)\, dy,\quad \omega_{\alpha}(y)=(1-y^2)^{\alpha},\quad \alpha >0
nodes.label: Eq1.1

nodes.name: Operator $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: They are also the eigenfunctions of the operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}=\frac{c}{2\pi}\mathcal F_c^{({\alpha})^*} \circ \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}},$ defined on $L^2{(I, \omega_{\alpha})}$ by \begin{equation} \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)} g (x) = \int_{-1}^1 \frac{c}{2 \pi}\mathcal K_{\alpha}(c(x-y)) g(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y) \, dy, \quad \mathcal K_{\alpha}(x)=\sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+1/2}\Gamma(\alpha+1) \frac{J_{\alpha+1/2}(x)}{x^{\alpha+1/2}}. \end{equation} Here $ J_{\alpha}(\cdot)$ is the Bessel function of the first kind and order $ \alpha>-1.$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}=\frac{c}{2\pi}\mathcal F^*\mathcal F$, an integral operator with a Bessel-function kernel on $L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Equation (6)
nodes.statement: \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)} g (x) = \int_{-1}^1 \frac{c}{2 \pi}\mathcal K_{\alpha}(c(x-y)) g(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y) \, dy, \quad \mathcal K_{\alpha}(x)=\sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+1/2}\Gamma(\alpha+1) \frac{J_{\alpha+1/2}(x)}{x^{\alpha+1/2}}.
nodes.label: EEq0

nodes.name: Eigenvalues $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$
nodes.statement: Moreover, the eigenvalues $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$ and $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ are related to each others by the identity ${\displaystyle \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)= \frac{c}{2\pi } |\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|^2}.$

nodes.name: Gegenbauer-type Sturm-Liouville operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: Note that the previous two integral operators commute with the following Gegenbauer-type Sturm-Liouville operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)},$ defined by $$ \mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} (f)(x)= -\frac{1}{\omega_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{d}{dx}\left[ \omega_{\alpha}(x) (1-x^2) f'(x)\right] +c^2 x^2 f(x),\quad \omega_{\alpha}(x)= (1-x^2)^{\alpha}.$$

nodes.name: Classical bounds on the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$
nodes.statement: Also, note that the $(n+1)-$th eigenvalue $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$ of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ satisfies the following classical inequalities, \begin{equation} n (n+2\alpha+1) \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n (n+2\alpha+1) +c^2,\quad \forall n\geq 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (7)
nodes.statement: n (n+2\alpha+1) \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n (n+2\alpha+1) +c^2,\quad \forall n\geq 0.
nodes.label: boundschi

nodes.name: GPSWFs $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ (notation)
nodes.statement: We will denote by$(\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)})_{n\geq 0},$ the set of the eigenfunctions of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}, \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ and $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}.$ They are called generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs).

nodes.name: GPSWFs form an orthogonal basis of $L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)$
nodes.statement: It has been shown that $ \{ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} , n\geq 0 \} $ is an orthogonal basis of $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}), I=[-1,1].$
conclusions: $ \{ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} , n\geq 0 \} $ is an orthogonal basis of $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}), I=[-1,1].$

nodes.name: Restricted Paley-Wiener space $B_c^{(\alpha)}$ of weighted $c$-band-limited functions
nodes.statement: We recall that the restricted Paley-Wiener space of weighted $c-$band-limited functions has been defined in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} by \begin{equation} B_c^{(\alpha)}=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c],\, \, \widehat f\in L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)\}. \end{equation} Here, $L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)$ is the weighted $L^2(-c,c)-$space with norm given by $$\| f\|^2_{L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)}= \int_{-c}^c |f(t)|^2 \omega_{-\alpha}\left(\frac{t}{c}\right)\, dt.$$

nodes.name: Equation (8)
nodes.statement: B_c^{(\alpha)}=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c],\, \, \widehat f\in L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)\}.
nodes.label: GBc

nodes.name: Super-exponential decay of $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ (Karoui-Souabni)
nodes.statement: It has been shown in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} that the eigenvalues $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ decay asymptotically at a super-exponential rate that is for $ 0<b<4/e$ there exists $N_b \in \mathbb{N}$ such that : \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) < e^{-2n \log(\frac{bn}{c})} \qquad \forall n \geq N_b, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For $0<b<4/e$, $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) < e^{-2n\log(bn/c)}$ for all large $n$.

nodes.name: Equation (9)
nodes.statement: \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) < e^{-2n \log(\frac{bn}{c})} \qquad \forall n \geq N_b,
nodes.label: decaylambda0

nodes.name: Second decay rate of $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ for $0<\alpha<3/2$
nodes.statement: More precisely, it has been shown in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2}, that if $c>0$ and $0<\alpha <\frac{3}{2}$, then there exist $N_{\alpha}(c)\in \mathbb N$ and a constant $C_{\alpha}>0$ such that \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq C_{\alpha} \exp\left(-(2n+1)\left[ \log\left(\frac{4n+4\alpha+2}{e c}\right)+ C_{\alpha} \frac{c^2}{2n+1}\right]\right),\quad \forall\, n\geq N_{\alpha}(c). \end{equation}
conclusions: there exist $N_{\alpha}(c)\in \mathbb N$ and a constant $C_{\alpha}>0$ such that
nodes.statement_short: For $0<\alpha<3/2$, $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)\le C_\alpha\exp(-(2n+1)[\log((4n+4\alpha+2)/(ec)) + C_\alpha c^2/(2n+1)])$ for large $n$.

nodes.name: Equation (10)
nodes.statement: \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq C_{\alpha} \exp\left(-(2n+1)\left[ \log\left(\frac{4n+4\alpha+2}{e c}\right)+ C_{\alpha} \frac{c^2}{2n+1}\right]\right),\quad \forall\, n\geq N_{\alpha}(c).
nodes.label: decay_lambda2

nodes.name: Jacobi-expansion scheme for computing the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: In \cite{Karoui-Souabni1}, the authors have proposed the following scheme for the computation of the GPSWFs. In fact, since $\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}\in L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha}),$ then its series expansion with respect to the Jacobi polynomials basis is given by \begin{equation} \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) =\sum_{k\geq 0} \beta_k^n \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k (x),\quad x\in [-1,1]. \end{equation} Here, $\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k$ denotes the normalized Jacobi polynomial of degree $k,$ given by \begin{equation} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{k}(x)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{h_k}}P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k(x),\quad h_k=\frac{2^{2\alpha+1}\Gamma^2(k+\alpha+1)}{k!(2k+2\alpha+1)\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}. \end{equation} The expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ as well as the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$ this system is given by \begin{eqnarray} \lefteqn{\frac{\sqrt{(k+1)(k+2)(k+2\alpha+1)(k+2\alpha+2)}}{(2k+2\alpha+3)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+5)(2k+2\alpha +1)}} c^2 \beta_{k+2}^n + \big( k(k+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \frac{2k(k+2\alpha+1)+2\alpha-1}{(2k+2\alpha+3)(2k+2\alpha-1)} \big) \beta_k^n}\nonumber \\ &&\hspace*{2cm} + \frac{\sqrt{k(k-1)(k+2\alpha)(k+2\alpha-1)}}{(2k+2\alpha-1)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+1)(2k+2\alpha-3)}} c^2 \beta_{k-2}^n= \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \beta_k^n, \quad k\geq 0. \end{eqnarray}
output: The expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ as well as the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ in normalized Jacobi polynomials; the coefficients $\beta_k^n$ and $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$ solve a tridiagonal eigensystem.

nodes.name: Equation (11)
nodes.statement: \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) =\sum_{k\geq 0} \beta_k^n \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k (x),\quad x\in [-1,1].
nodes.label: expansion1

nodes.name: Normalized Jacobi polynomial $\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k$
nodes.statement: Here, $\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k$ denotes the normalized Jacobi polynomial of degree $k,$ given by \begin{equation} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{k}(x)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{h_k}}P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k(x),\quad h_k=\frac{2^{2\alpha+1}\Gamma^2(k+\alpha+1)}{k!(2k+2\alpha+1)\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (12)
nodes.statement: \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{k}(x)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{h_k}}P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k(x),\quad h_k=\frac{2^{2\alpha+1}\Gamma^2(k+\alpha+1)}{k!(2k+2\alpha+1)\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}.
nodes.label: JacobiP

nodes.name: Eigensystem for the expansion coefficients
nodes.statement: \lefteqn{\frac{\sqrt{(k+1)(k+2)(k+2\alpha+1)(k+2\alpha+2)}}{(2k+2\alpha+3)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+5)(2k+2\alpha +1)}} c^2 \beta_{k+2}^n + \big( k(k+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \frac{2k(k+2\alpha+1)+2\alpha-1}{(2k+2\alpha+3)(2k+2\alpha-1)} \big) \beta_k^n}\nonumber \\ &&\hspace*{2cm} + \frac{\sqrt{k(k-1)(k+2\alpha)(k+2\alpha-1)}}{(2k+2\alpha-1)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+1)(2k+2\alpha-3)}} c^2 \beta_{k-2}^n= \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \beta_k^n, \quad k\geq 0.
nodes.label: eigensystem

nodes.name: Expand in the Jacobi basis
nodes.statement: In fact, since $\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}\in L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha}),$ then its series expansion with respect to the Jacobi polynomials basis is given by \begin{equation} \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) =\sum_{k\geq 0} \beta_k^n \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k (x),\quad x\in [-1,1]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}=\sum_k\beta_k^n\widetilde P_k^{(\alpha,\alpha)}$.

nodes.name: Solve the eigensystem for the coefficients
nodes.statement: The expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ as well as the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$ this system is given by \begin{eqnarray} \lefteqn{\frac{\sqrt{(k+1)(k+2)(k+2\alpha+1)(k+2\alpha+2)}}{(2k+2\alpha+3)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+5)(2k+2\alpha +1)}} c^2 \beta_{k+2}^n + \big( k(k+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \frac{2k(k+2\alpha+1)+2\alpha-1}{(2k+2\alpha+3)(2k+2\alpha-1)} \big) \beta_k^n}\nonumber \\ &&\hspace*{2cm} + \frac{\sqrt{k(k-1)(k+2\alpha)(k+2\alpha-1)}}{(2k+2\alpha-1)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+1)(2k+2\alpha-3)}} c^2 \beta_{k-2}^n= \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \beta_k^n, \quad k\geq 0. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $\beta_k^n$ and $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$ as eigenvectors/eigenvalues of a three-term (step 2) recurrence system.

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $H^r_\alpha$ for real $r$ (interpolation)
nodes.statement: For any real r, we define the weighted Sobolev space $H^r_{\alpha}$ by interpolation $ H^r_{\alpha} = \Big[H^{[r]}_{\alpha},H^{[r]+1}_{\alpha}\Big]$ as it is done in \cite{Bergh-Lofstrom} and \cite{Bernardi-Maday}

nodes.name: Space $\mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I)$ of infinitely differentiable functions
nodes.statement: We denote by $ \mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I) $ the set of infinitely differentiable functions defined on $ I $.

nodes.name: Sobolev space $H_0^s(I)$
nodes.statement: Let $H_0^s(I) $ be the completion of $ \mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I) $ in $H^s(I)$. $H_0^s(I) $ is a Hilbert space under the inner product. For $s\geq 0$, we define $H_0^s(I) $by interpolation as in \cite{Bergh-Lofstrom} and \cite{Bernardi-Maday}.

nodes.name: Super-exponential decay of the eigenvalues of the weighted finite Fourier transform (Theorem 3)

nodes.name: Recall the min-max principle
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof:} We first recall the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle concerning the eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal G,$ with positive eigenvalues arranged in the decreasing order $\lambda_0\geq \lambda_1\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_n\geq \cdots ,$ then we have $$\lambda_n = \min_{f\in S_n}\,\,\, \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\|f\|_{\mathcal G}=1} < Tf, f>_{\mathcal G},$$ where $S_n$ is a subspace of $\mathcal G$ of dimension $n.$
nodes.statement_short: Recall the Courant-Fischer-Weyl min-max characterization of eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Choose the test subspace
nodes.statement: In our case, we have $T=\mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},$ $\mathcal G= L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}).$ We consider the special case of $$S_n=\mbox{Span}\left\{\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_0, \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_1,\ldots,\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{n-1}\right\}$$ and $$f=\displaystyle\sum_{k\geq n} a_k \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k \in S_n^{\perp},\qquad \parallel f\parallel_{L^2_{(I,\omega_\alpha)}}=\displaystyle\sum_{k\geq n}|a_k|^2=1.$$ Here the $ \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_{k} $ are the normalized Jacobi polynomials given by \eqref{JacobiP}.
nodes.statement_short: Take $S_n$ spanned by the first $n$ normalized Jacobi polynomials and $f\in S_n^\perp$ of unit norm.

nodes.name: Recall Fourier transform of Jacobi polynomials
nodes.statement: From [\cite{NIST} page 456], we have \begin{equation} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} = \parallel \sqrt{\pi} \left(\frac{2}{cx}\right) ^{\alpha+1/2} \frac{\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\Gamma(k+1)}J_{k+\alpha+1/2}(cx) \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \parallel x^k \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}^2=\beta(k+1/2,\alpha+1)\leq \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{e}}\frac{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}{k^{\alpha+1}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Express $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}P_k$ via Bessel functions and bound $\|x^k\|$ by a Beta function.

nodes.name: Apply the Bessel bound
nodes.statement: By using the well-known bound of the Bessel function given by \begin{equation} |J_{\alpha}(x)|\leq \frac{|x|^{\alpha}}{2^{\alpha}\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\forall\alpha>-1/2, \;\; \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \end{equation} one gets, \begin{eqnarray} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\sqrt{h_k}\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(k+\alpha+3/2)}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k} \parallel x^k \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}. \nonumber\\ &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\sqrt{h_k}\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(k+\alpha+3/2)}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k}\left(\frac{\pi}{e}\right)^{1/4}\frac{\sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the bound $|J_\alpha(x)|\le |x|^\alpha/(2^\alpha\Gamma(\alpha+1))$.

nodes.name: Apply Gamma function inequalities
nodes.statement: Next, we use \eqref{JacobiP} and the following useful inequalities for the Gamma function, see \cite{Batir} \begin{equation} \sqrt{2e}\left(\frac{x+1/2}{e}\right)^{x+1/2}\leq\Gamma(x+1)\leq \sqrt{2\pi}\left(\frac{x+1/2}{e}\right)^{x+1/2}\;,\;\;\; x>0. \end{equation} Then, we have \begin{eqnarray} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\sqrt{(k+\alpha+\frac{1}{2})\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}}{2^{\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\Gamma(k+1)}\Gamma(k+\alpha+\frac{3}{2})}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k}\left(\frac{\pi}{e}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\frac{\sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\big(k+2\alpha+\frac{1}{2}\Big)^{\frac{k}{2}+\alpha+\frac{1}{4 }}}{\sqrt{ec}2^{\alpha}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}\left(k+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{k}{2}+\frac{1}{4}}\left(k+\alpha+1\right)^{k+\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}} \left(\frac{ce}{2}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2 }}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}2^{\alpha}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\left(1+\frac{\alpha-\frac{1}{2}}{k+\alpha+1}\right)^{\frac{k}{2}+\alpha+\frac{1}{4}} \left(\frac{ce}{2k+1}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2}}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Use Batir's Gamma inequalities to simplify the bound.

nodes.name: Monotonicity simplification
nodes.statement: Since the function $g_a(x)=\left(1+\frac{a}{x}\right)^{a+x}$ for $x\geq1$ and $a>-1$ is decreasing on $[1,+\infty[$. Then, we have \begin{eqnarray} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq &\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{c}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \left(\frac{ce}{2k+1}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2}}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Use monotonicity of $(1+a/x)^{a+x}$ to get bound (24).

nodes.name: Bound the quadratic form
nodes.statement: Hence, For the previous $f\in S_n^{\perp},$ and by using H\"older's inequality, combined with the Minkowski's inequality for an infinite sums, and taking into account that $\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}= 1,$ so that $|a_k|\leq 1,$ for $k\geq n,$ one gets: \begin{eqnarray} |< \mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f,f>_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}|&=&|< \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f,\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}f>_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}| \leq \sum_{k\geq n} |a_k|^2 \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k\|^2_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}\\ &\leq&\left(\frac{2^\frac{1}{4}\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}} \sum_{k\geq n} \left(\frac{ec}{2k+1}\right)^{k+1/2}\frac{1}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\right)^2 \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Holder and Minkowski bound $\langle Tf,f\rangle$ by a squared tail sum.

nodes.name: Compare sum with integral
nodes.statement: The decay of the sequence appearing in the previous sum, allows us to compare this later with its integral counterpart, that is \begin{equation} \sum_{k\geq n} \left(\frac{ec}{2k+1}\right)^{k+1/2}\frac{1}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \leq \int_{n-1}^{\infty}\frac{ e^{-(x+1/2) \log(\frac{2x+1}{ec})}}{x^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\, dx\leq \int_{n-1}^{\infty}\frac{ e^{-(x+1/2)\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}}{(n-1)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\, dx. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compare the tail sum with an integral.

nodes.name: Combine the bounds
nodes.statement: Hence, by using (\ref{Eq3.3}) and (\ref{Eq3.4}), one concludes that \begin{eqnarray} \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\, \|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})=1}} < \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f, \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f>^{1/2}_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}&\leq &\frac{2^\frac{1}{4}\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}} \frac{1}{\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n-1/2}\frac{1}{(n-1)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\nonumber\\ &\leq&\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)} \left(\frac{2}{ec}\right)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{2}} \frac{1}{\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}} \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound the max over $S_n^\perp$.

nodes.name: Conclude with min-max
nodes.statement: To conclude the proof of the theorem, it suffices to use the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle.$\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by the min-max principle.

nodes.name: Improvement over earlier decay rates
nodes.statement: The decay rate given by the last proposition improve the two results mentioned above \eqref{decaylambda0} and \eqref{decay_lambda2}. Indeed, we have a more precise result furthermore the proof given in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2} contains two serious drawbacks. It is only valid in the particular case $0 < \alpha < 3/2 $ and clearly more sophisticated than the previous one.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3 improves the earlier decay bounds of Karoui-Souabni with a simpler proof valid for all $\alpha\ge0$.

nodes.name: ODE satisfied by the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: \omega_{\alpha}(x)\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} \psi(x)+w_{\alpha}(x)\chi_{n,\alpha}\psi(x)= ( w_{\alpha}(x)\psi'(x)(1-x^2))'+ w_{\alpha}(x)(\chi_{n}^{\alpha}-c^2 x^2)\psi(x)=0,\quad x\in [-1,1].

nodes.name: Incomplete elliptic integral $S(x)$
nodes.statement: As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui2}, we consider the incomplete elliptic integral \begin{equation} S(x)=\int_x^1 \sqrt{\frac{1-qt^2}{1-t^2}}\, dt,\qquad q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)}<1. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Liouville transform $\psi=\phi_\alpha V(S)$
nodes.statement: Then, we write $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ into the form \begin{equation} \psi(x)=\phi_{\alpha}(x)V(S(x)),\qquad \phi_{\alpha}(x)=(1-x^2)^{(-1-2\alpha)/4} (1-qx^2)^{-1/4}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (29)
nodes.statement: \psi(x)=\phi_{\alpha}(x)V(S(x)),\qquad \phi_{\alpha}(x)=(1-x^2)^{(-1-2\alpha)/4} (1-qx^2)^{-1/4}.

nodes.name: ODE satisfied by $V$ after the Liouville transform
nodes.statement: By combining (\ref{eq2_diff}), (\ref{Liouvile_transform2}) and using straightforward computations, it can be easily checked that $V(\cdot)$ satisfies the following second order differential equation \begin{equation} V''(s)+\left(\chi_{n,\alpha}+\theta_{\alpha}(s)\right)V(s)=0,\quad s\in [0, S(0)] \end{equation} with $$ \theta_{\alpha}(S(x))=(w_{\alpha}(x)(1-x^2)\phi_{\alpha}'(x))'\frac{1}{\phi_{\alpha}(x)w_{\alpha}(x)(1-qx^2)}.$$
conclusions: $V(\cdot)$ satisfies the following second order differential equation
nodes.statement_short: After the Liouville transform, $V$ solves $V''+(\chi_{n,\alpha}+\theta_\alpha)V=0$ with an explicit potential $\theta_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Equation (30)
nodes.statement: V''(s)+\left(\chi_{n,\alpha}+\theta_{\alpha}(s)\right)V(s)=0,\quad s\in [0, S(0)]

nodes.name: Function $Q_\alpha$
nodes.statement: Define $ Q_{\alpha}(x)=w_{\alpha}(x)^2(1-x^2)(1-qx^2),$ then we have ${\displaystyle \frac{\phi_{\alpha}'(x)}{\phi_{\alpha}(x)}=-1/4 \frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}. }$

nodes.name: Explicit form of the potential $\theta_\alpha$
nodes.statement: It follows that $\theta_{\alpha}(s)$ can be written as \begin{equation} \theta_{\alpha}(S(x))=\frac{1}{16(1-qx^2)}\Big[\Big(\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)^2(1-x^2)-4\frac{d}{dx}\Big((1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)-4(1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\Big]. \end{equation} Since $ Q_{\alpha}(x)=w_{\alpha}^2(x)Q_0(x),$ then we have ${\displaystyle \frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}=2\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}+\frac{Q_0'(x)}{Q_0(x)}} $ and ${\displaystyle \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}=-\frac{2\alpha x}{1-x^2}.} $ Hence, we have \begin{eqnarray} \theta_{\alpha}(S(x)) &=&\theta_0(S(x))+\frac{-1}{4(1-qx^2)}\Big[ \big(\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\big)^2 (1-x^2)+2\frac{d}{dx}[(1-x^2)\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}] \Big] \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{1}{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\Big( -\alpha^2 x^2 + \alpha (1-x^2) \Big) \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{(1-qx^2)}-\frac{\alpha^2}{(1-q x^2)(1-x^2)}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Computation expressing $\theta_\alpha(S(x))$ as $\theta_0(S(x))$ plus explicit $\alpha$-dependent terms.

nodes.name: Equation (31)
nodes.statement: \theta_{\alpha}(S(x))=\frac{1}{16(1-qx^2)}\Big[\Big(\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)^2(1-x^2)-4\frac{d}{dx}\Big((1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)-4(1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\Big].

nodes.name: Equation (32)
nodes.statement: \theta_{\alpha}(S(x)) &=&\theta_0(S(x))+\frac{-1}{4(1-qx^2)}\Big[ \big(\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\big)^2 (1-x^2)+2\frac{d}{dx}[(1-x^2)\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}] \Big] \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{1}{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\Big( -\alpha^2 x^2 + \alpha (1-x^2) \Big) \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{(1-qx^2)}-\frac{\alpha^2}{(1-q x^2)(1-x^2)}.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\theta_\alpha(S(x))$
nodes.statement: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q=c^2/\chi_n^{\alpha}(c) <\frac{3}{17}$, we have $\theta_{\alpha}(S(x))$ is increasing on $ [0.1]$.\\

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof:} We use the notation $u=1-x^2$ and with straightforward computations, we have \begin{eqnarray*} (\theta_{\alpha}(S(x)))'&=&(\theta_{0}(S(x)))'+\frac{2x}{(1-qx^2)^2(1-x^2)^2}\left[q\alpha(\alpha+1)(1-x^2)^2 -q\alpha^2(1-x^2)-\alpha^2(1-qx^2)\right] \\ &=& \frac{2xH(u)}{4u^2(1-q+qu)^4} \end{eqnarray*} where \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &=& G(u)+4(1-q+qu^2)^2[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]\\ &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2[G(u)+4[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]] \end{eqnarray*} with $G(u)\geq\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))\geq0,\;\;\forall q>0,\;\;\alpha>0$ then \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[ \frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))+4[-q\frac{\alpha^3}{\alpha+1}-(1-q)\alpha^2]\right] \\ &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2\left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)u\right]. \end{eqnarray*} Then if $0\leq q\leq\frac{3}{17}$ and $\alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2 \left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)\right]\nonumber\\ &\geq &(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(1+13q)-4\alpha^2\right]\geq0 \end{eqnarray*} $\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation of the derivative in $u=1-x^2$; a lower bound on the numerator $H(u)$ is nonnegative when $q\le 3/17$ and $\alpha\le 1/4$.

nodes.name: Local estimate of the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and for any integer $n\in \mathbb N,$ with $0<q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)} <\frac{3}{17}$, we have \begin{equation} \displaystyle{\sup_{x\in[0,1]}}\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\omega_{\alpha}(x)|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x)|^2\leq|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0)|^2+ \frac{|{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)|^2}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)}= A^2 \leq 2 \alpha + 1 \; \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Weighted uniform bound on $|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}|^2$ on $[0,1]$ by its value and derivative at $0$, at most $2\alpha+1$.

nodes.name: Equation (33)
nodes.statement: \displaystyle{\sup_{x\in[0,1]}}\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\omega_{\alpha}(x)|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x)|^2\leq|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0)|^2+ \frac{|{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)|^2}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)}= A^2 \leq 2 \alpha + 1 \;

nodes.statement: For $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$ ,we have $ \theta_{\alpha} \circ S $ is increasing. Since $S$ is decreasing then $ \theta $ is also decreasing. nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: By differentiating with respect to $c$ the differential equation satisfied by GPSWFs , one gets $$ (1-x^2) \partial_c {{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'}'(x) - 2(\alpha+1)x \partial_c {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(x) + (\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-c^2x^2) \partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$ Hence, we have $$ \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$ It's well known that $\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c $ is a self-adjoint operator and have $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ as eigenfunctions . Hence, we have $$ < \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}; \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}>_{\omega_{\alpha}} = 0 $$ It follows that $$ \int_{-1}^{1} \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}} ^{2}(x) dx = 0. $$ From the fact that $ \norm{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} = 1 $, one gets \begin{equation} \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) = 2c \int_{-1}^{1} x^2 {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \end{equation} As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui1}, we denote by $ A= \Bigg[\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) + \frac{{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)} \Bigg]^{1/2} $ and consider the auxiliary function $$ K_n(t) = - (1-t^2)^{2\alpha+1} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2 - \frac{(1-t^2)^{2\alpha+2}}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)(1-qt^2)}({\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}')^2 $$ Straightforward computations give us $$ K'_n(t) = 2(2\alpha+1)t(1-t^2)^{2\alpha} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) - {H(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(t)}^2 $$ with $ H(t) \geq 0 $ for $t\in[0,1]$. Hence $$ K'_n(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}^2(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t). $$ So one has the inequality \begin{equation} K_n(1) - K_n(0) = A^2 \leq 2(2\alpha+1) \int_{0}^{1} t{|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |}^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \leq (2\alpha+1) \Bigg[\int_{-1}^{1}t^2 |\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \Bigg] ^{1/2}. \end{equation} That is \begin{equation} A^2 \leq (2\alpha+1) B^{1/2}. \end{equation} Remark that \eqref{estimation} implies that \begin{equation} 1-B \leq 2 A^2 \end{equation} By combining \eqref{11} and \eqref{12} we conclude that $B^{1/2} $ is bounded below by the largest solution of the equation $ X^2 + 2(2\alpha+1) X -1 = 0 $
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the eigen-equation in $c$ to get $\partial_c\chi_n=2cB$; an auxiliary function $K_n$ gives $A^2\le(2\alpha+1)B^{1/2}$, combined with Lemma 2 to bound $B$ below.
